title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page continues 'n°445' on the scheme G_{ρ,σ} of solutions (α, β, μ) of the 'loop equation' (équation des lacets). Here ρ and σ are fixed torsion matrices in GL_2, and S is the base.

The previous page proved an isomorphism B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ ≅ G_{ρ,σ}, with T_ρ and T_σ the centraliser tori of ρ and σ. Here T_ρ consists of the invertible elements cρ+d of O_S[ρ]. Concretely, there are unique a ∈ T_ρ and b ∈ T_σ with αa, βb ∈ ΓB'_0. One then has αa = βb =: u and (α, β, μ) = (u a^{-1}, u b^{-1}, det u).

The page restates this in terms of α alone:
- a = c_0ρ + d_0 (91) and b = t_0σ + u_0 (92), with coefficients that are sections of O_S determined by α (resp. β).
- (93): αa = βb = u.

It then makes everything explicit in the 'modular case' ρ = (0 1; −1 1) (order 6, image of order 3 in PSL_2) and σ = (0 −1; 1 0) (order 4). Writing α = (a b; c d) and β = (r s; t u) gives:
- (94): a = (cρ+d)/(c²+cd+d²).
- (95): b = (tσ+u)/(t²+u²).

The denominators are the norms N(cρ+d) = det(cρ+d) = c²+cd+d² (Eisenstein-type form) and det(tσ+u) = t²+u² (Gaussian form). He identifies them with δ times an entry of ξ = αρα^{-1} (resp. δ' times an entry of η = βσβ^{-1}).

Check: α(cρ+d) = (δ, ac+bc+bd; 0, c²+cd+d²). Dividing by c²+cd+d² gives an upper-triangular matrix with (2,2)-entry 1, so B'_0 is the 'affine' Borel {(x y; 0 1)}.

A marginal note says he would like these formulas recovered in the general case. The page ends by noting the one obstacle to matching these with the 'brutal' calculations of p. 398' (75)(78): a factor τ_∞^α tied to a Z/2 invariant. The next page resolves this by observing that the earlier loop equation allowed a sign, ξ = ε η ℓ_1^ν, whereas the present theory assumes ε = +1.

The purpose is to parametrise explicitly the solutions of the loop equations attached to the modular group PSL_2(Z) = Z/3 * Z/2 (the base case of the Teichmüller tower in the Longue Marche programme), as a product of a Borel-type group and two non-split tori.
errors: Formula (95) has a sign error with σ = (0 −1; 1 0) and B'_0 upper-triangular, as forced by the (correct) check of (94). β(tσ+u) has lower-left entry 2tu ≠ 0. The correct choice is b = (u − tσ)/(t²+u²) = (tσ^{-1}+u)/(t²+u²): then β·b has lower row (0, 1). Grothendieck himself flags the formulas 'sauf erreur'.

The identifications 'δD = c²+cd+d²' and 'δ'U = t²+u²' do not match the entries named. With ξ = αρα^{-1} one finds δ·C = −(c²+cd+d²), i.e. the lower-left entry up to sign. Likewise δ'·T = t²+u², again the lower-left entry, whereas δD = ac+ad+bd. So the relevant coefficient is the lower-left one (C, resp. T), not the diagonal D, U.
(93) appears as 'α a^{-1} = β b' in the image/transcription. By (88)–(89) of the previous page it should read α a = β b (= u); the exponent is a slip.

ideas.what: Parametrisation of the solution scheme of the loop equation for (ρ, σ) as B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ, made explicit via norm forms c²+cd+d² and t²+u² of the CM tori Z[ρ] (Eisenstein) and Z[σ] (Gaussian)
ideas.modern_name: torus-torsor / Iwasawa-type decomposition of the space of pairs of conjugates of elliptic elements of SL_2; CM tori at j=0 and j=1728
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (elliptic points of PSL_2(Z)); the loop-equation framework is Grothendieck's own (related to the defining relations of Drinfeld's GT, 1990)
ideas.where_published: Only the general programme is in Esquisse d'un programme / La Longue Marche (unsure for the explicit computation)

ideas.what: Recognition that the earlier loop equation contained a sign ε (ξ = ε η ℓ_1^ν), responsible for the factor τ_∞; the 'simpler' theory takes ε = +1
ideas.modern_name: central sign ambiguity SL_2 vs PSL_2 / lifting of the relations of Z/3 * Z/2

deep.surprise_reason: Routine explicit 2×2 matrix computation inside Grothendieck's private loop-equation formalism. It contains a sign slip, and nothing on the page constitutes an unrecorded result or connection.
transcription_corrections: (93) is likely meant as α a = β b (= u); the superscript on a looks like a slip, consistent with (88)–(89) of p. 286.
In the annotations to (94)/(95), the named coefficient is mathematically the lower-left entry C (resp. T) of ξ (resp. η), not D (resp. U). The handwriting should be rechecked.
The marginal note reads roughly 'Je voudrais [voir] ces formules retrouvées dans le cas général'.
The last line refers to the factor τ_∞^α of p. 398' (78) with α ∈ Z/2Z (crossed-out α_2(μ)), in the case α = 1.
